chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Azdi, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, for Allah are angels assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So when a man intends to visit him and performs ritual bath, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) calls out to him: 'O caravan of Allah, rejoice in accompanying me in Paradise.' And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) calls out to him: 'I am guarantor for the fulfillment of your needs and the repulsion of calamity from you in this world and the Hereafter.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) surround them on their right and left sides until they return to their families.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and promises for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt in the spiritual journey of the Zayyar, framing the visit as a divine audience. It underscores the Shia belief in the active, protective presence of the Prophet and Imam Ali, who escort the pilgrim, thereby linking the physical act of purification (ghusl) with metaphysical assurance of needs being met and calamities averted.
